title:
You're a civil servant.
*How do you buy right?*

lines.say: You are a civil servant. You want a home that makes money. But you can't use anything you learned at work.
lines.cap: you are a civil servant. you want profit, but *nothing from work*

lines.say: This month, eight officers were referred to the police over purchases near future MRT stations. The Minister stressed a referral does not mean wrongdoing.
lines.cap: 8 officers referred to police. *a referral does not mean wrongdoing*

lines.say: So what's left? The same public data everyone has. Used better.
lines.cap: what's left? *the same public data, used better*

lines.say: One. The Master Plan. URA publishes what every area is zoned for, years ahead. Look for areas where the plan is visible, but the amenities aren't built yet.
lines.cap: 1: the Master Plan. *plan visible, amenities not built yet*

lines.say: Two. Land prices. When developers pay high for land, future launches can't go cheap. Buy below the next launch.
lines.cap: 2: land prices. high land cost means *future launches can't go cheap*

lines.say: Three. The entry window. When MOP or TOP releases many sellers at once, buyers get leverage.
lines.cap: 3: the entry window. many sellers at once = *buyer leverage*

lines.say: Four. Buy below a tested exit. If similar units have already sold higher, your profit doesn't depend on any announcement.
None of this needs inside information. Just discipline.
Which would you use first? Comment plan, land, window, or exit.
lines.cap: which first? comment *PLAN, LAND, WINDOW or EXIT*

caption:
You're a civil servant. You want your home to make money, but you can't use anything from work. 🏛️

Here are four public signals anyone can read: URA's Master Plan, land sale prices, MOP/TOP seller windows, and buying below a tested exit. None of them need inside information.

Which would you use first? Comment PLAN, LAND, WINDOW or EXIT 👇
